p.src: Now Song Jiang, wishing to recover the bodies of Xie Zhen and Xie Bao, went to the foot of Wulong Ridge and fell squarely into Shi Bao’s trap. Ambushers rose on every side: Shi Bao’s troops barred the way ahead, while Deng Yuanjue cut off the road of retreat behind. Shi Bao shouted fiercely, “Song Jiang, if you do not dismount and surrender now, what are you waiting for?” Guan Sheng flew into a rage, spurred his horse forward, and swung his blade at Shi Bao. Before the contest between the two generals was decided, fresh battle cries arose from the rear. Behind them, the four naval commanders had all come ashore and, joining Wang Ji and Chao Zhong, charged down from the ridge. Hua Rong hurried out to hold the rear and engaged Wang Ji in combat. After fighting countless bouts, Hua Rong turned and fled. Wang Ji and Chao Zhong pursued their advantage, but Hua Rong wheeled around, swiftly loosed two arrows in succession, and struck both generals, tumbling them from their horses. The troops raised a great cry, but dared not advance and turned in retreat. Seeing Wang Ji and Chao Zhong shot dead one after the other, the four naval commanders dared not advance; thus Hua Rong succeeded in holding them at bay. Then two more columns of troops burst out from the flank: one led by Commander Bai Qin, the other by Commander Jing De. Two generals rode out together from Song Jiang’s formation: Lü Fang met Bai Qin in combat, while Guo Sheng held Jing De at bay. Fighting broke out in every quarter, each side battling desperately against the other. Just as Song Jiang was in dire distress, he heard battle cries rising to the heavens behind the southern army, and saw its troops fleeing. It was Li Kui, leading the two shield fighters—Xiang Chong and Li Gun—and a thousand infantrymen in an attack upon the rear of Shi Bao’s cavalry. Deng Yuanjue was about to lead his men to the rescue when Lu Zhishen and Wu Song crashed into his rear. Two monastic sabers hacked crosswise and hewed straight down, while a solid-iron monk’s staff thrust and jabbed; the two men led a thousand infantrymen directly into the fray. Behind them came Qin Ming, Li Ying, Zhu Tong, Yan Shun, Ma Lin, Fan Rui, Yizhangqing, and Wang Aihu, each leading cavalry or infantry and charging in recklessly, cutting men down. The Song troops attacked from all four sides and scattered the forces of Shi Bao and Deng Yuanjue. They rescued Song Jiang and the others and returned to Tonglu County, while Shi Bao too gathered his troops and withdrew up the ridge. Back in camp, Song Jiang thanked the generals, saying, “Had my brothers not come to my rescue, I, Song Jiang, would already be a ghost beneath the springs together with Xie Zhen and Xie Bao.” Wu Yong said, “Your going there did not accord with my poor judgment. Fearing some mishap, I sent the generals to reinforce you.” Song Jiang thanked them again and again.

p.src: Meanwhile, on Wulong Ridge, the two marshals Shi Bao and Deng Yuanjue conferred in their stronghold: “At present Song Jiang’s army has withdrawn and is encamped in Tonglu County. If they should secretly cross by some bypath and get beyond the ridge, Muzhou, being close at hand, would be in grave danger. It would be better for the Imperial Preceptor to go in person to the inner court at Qingxi, seek audience with His Majesty, and request additional troops to guard this mountain pass. Then it can be held for the long term.” Deng Yuanjue said, “Your words are entirely right, Marshal. This humble monk will go at once.” Deng Yuanjue mounted at once and first went to Muzhou, where he met Right Chancellor Zu Shiyuan and said, “Song Jiang’s soldiers are powerful and his men fierce; their onslaught is irresistible. His army is sweeping onward, and I truly fear that disaster may befall us. I have come expressly to petition for more troops and generals to defend the pass.” On hearing this, Zu Shiyuan mounted with Deng Yuanjue. They left Muzhou and went together to Bangyuan Cave in Qingxi County, where they first met Left Chancellor Lou Minzhong, explained the matter, and requested that additional troops be dispatched. At the morning audience the next day, Fang La ascended the throne. The two chancellors and Deng Yuanjue entered together, performed their court obeisances, and when these were concluded, Deng Yuanjue stepped forward, wished His Majesty long life, and memorialized: “Your monk-subject Yuanjue received the imperial command to defend Hangzhou together with the Crown Prince. Unexpectedly, Song Jiang’s army, with its mighty troops and valiant generals, swept upon us. Its force was too great to withstand. Assessor Yuan lured them into the city, bringing about the fall of Hangzhou, while the Crown Prince, too eager for battle, sallied forth and met his death. Now Yuanjue and Marshal Shi Bao have withdrawn to defend the pass at Wulong Ridge. In recent days we have slain four of Song Jiang’s generals in succession, greatly restoring our prestige. Song Jiang has now advanced to Tonglu and encamped there. I truly fear that sooner or later the rebels may secretly cross by some bypath, break through the pass, and make the ridge impossible to hold. I beg Your Majesty to choose able generals without delay and dispatch additional elite troops to help defend the pass at Wulong Ridge, so that we may drive back the rebels and recover the lost cities.” Fang La said, “All the troops from every quarter have already been called up. Recently, because the pass on Yu Ridge in Shezhou was under severe threat, another several tens of thousands of troops were sent there. Only the Imperial Guard remains, and I need it to protect the inner palace. How could I disperse and dispatch it elsewhere?” Deng Yuanjue memorialized again: “If Your Majesty sends no relief troops, there is nothing your monk-subject can do. Once the Song troops cross the ridge, how can Muzhou possibly be defended?” Left Chancellor Lou Minzhong stepped from the ranks and memorialized: “The pass at Wulong Ridge is also a place of vital importance. I know that the Imperial Guard numbers thirty thousand in all. Ten thousand can be detached to accompany the Imperial Preceptor and defend the pass. I beg my king to consider this with sagacious judgment.” Fang La refused to heed Lou Minzhong’s counsel and steadfastly declined to dispatch any of the Imperial Guard to the relief of Wulong Ridge. When the court audience ended that day, everyone left the inner palace. Chancellor Lou then consulted with the officials and instructed Chancellor Zu to select one general in Muzhou and assign five thousand troops to accompany the Imperial Preceptor in defending Wulong Ridge. Accordingly, Deng Yuanjue returned to Muzhou with Zu Shiyuan, selected five thousand elite troops under a commander named Xiahou Cheng, and went back to the stronghold on Wulong Ridge, where he told Shi Bao what had happened. Shi Bao said, “Since the court will not dispatch the Imperial Guard, we must hold the pass for the time being and refrain from giving battle. Have the four naval commanders keep close guard over the riverbank at the head of the shoals. Whenever any boats approach, they are to drive them back, but they must not advance their own forces.”

p.src: Let us say no more for now of the Imperial Preceptor Radiant Treasure and the four others—Shi Bao, Bai Qin, Jing De, and Xiahou Cheng—guarding the pass at Black Dragon Ridge. Song Jiang, having lost a number of his officers, remained encamped in Tonglu County and held his troops in check without advancing. He stayed there for more than twenty days without going out to fight. Suddenly a scout rode in to report: “The court has again dispatched Privy Councillor Tong with rewards, and he has already reached Hangzhou. On learning that the army had divided into two columns, Privy Councillor Tong sent the general Wang Bing onward with a share of the rewards to Commander Lu’s forces at Yuling Pass. Privy Councillor Tong himself will arrive presently, bringing the remaining rewards.” Upon receiving the report, Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and the other commanders went twenty li beyond the county town to welcome him. They returned to the county offices, where the imperial edict was read aloud and the rewards were distributed among the commanders. Song Jiang and the others paid their respects to Privy Councillor Tong, then immediately held a banquet in his honor. Privy Councillor Tong asked, “I have heard many reports that officers have been lost during this campaign.” Song Jiang replied through his tears: “In former years, when we followed Chancellor Zhao on the northern campaign against the Liao, our soldiers and commanders won every battle, and truly not a single officer was lost. But ever since we received the edict to campaign against Fang La, Gongsun Sheng left us before we had even departed the capital, several others were retained in the imperial presence, and after we crossed the river on our advance, we lost several men at every place we reached. Recently another eight or nine officers fell ill in Hangzhou, and we do not yet know whether they will live or die. In the two recent battles at Black Dragon Ridge, we lost several more commanders. The mountains are precipitous and the waters swift, making it difficult to form battle lines, and we cannot break through the pass at short notice. Just as we were beset with anxiety, it was our good fortune that Your Excellency arrived.” Privy Councillor Tong said, “His present Majesty knows well of the great achievements won by the commanders. When he later heard that officers had been lost, he specially dispatched me with the generals Wang Bing and Zhao Tan to reinforce you. I have already sent Wang Bing with rewards to Commander Lu, to distribute them among his officers.” He then summoned Zhao Tan and introduced him to Song Jiang and the others, and they all encamped in Tonglu County. The banquet and entertainment then came to an end.

p.src: The next day, Privy Councillor Tong mustered the troops, intending to attack the pass at Black Dragon Ridge. Wu Yong remonstrated, “Your Excellency must not act rashly. First send Yan Shun and Ma Lin along the secluded paths by the streams to seek out local villagers, ask them the way, and find some other narrow trail by which we may cross to the far side of the pass. If we attack from both sides, the enemy will be unable to support one another, and the pass will fall into our hands with ease.” Song Jiang said, “That is an excellent plan.” He immediately sent Ma Lin and Yan Shun with several dozen sturdy soldiers to visit the villages and ask the inhabitants for directions. After being gone all day, they returned at dusk, bringing an old man before Song Jiang. Song Jiang asked, “Who is this old gentleman?” Ma Lin replied, “This old man is a native resident of the district and knows all the roads, streams, and hills hereabouts.” Song Jiang said, “Old sir, if you will show me a road across Black Dragon Ridge, I shall reward you handsomely.” The old man replied, “My family has lived here for generations. The people have repeatedly suffered Fang La’s ravages and have nowhere to flee. By good fortune the imperial army has arrived, bringing blessings to all the people and allowing us to see peace restored. I can show you a narrow path: once across Black Dragon Ridge, you will reach Dongguan, and from there Muzhou is not far. It leads to the north gate, then turns around to the west gate, which is at Black Dragon Ridge.” Song Jiang was delighted to hear this. He immediately ordered silver and valuables brought forth to reward the old guide, kept him in the camp, and had food and wine served to him. The next day, Song Jiang asked Privy Councillor Tong to remain and guard Tonglu County, while he himself set out along the narrow path with twelve senior and junior commanders. The twelve were Hua Rong, Qin Ming, Lu Zhishen, Wu Song, Dai Zong, Li Kui, Fan Rui, Wang Ying, Hu Sanniang, Xiang Chong, Li Gun, and Ling Zhen. Ten thousand cavalry and infantry accompanied them, following the old guide onward. The bells were removed from the horses’ bridles, and the soldiers hurried onward with gags between their teeth. When they reached Little Ox Ridge, a band of soldiers was already blocking the road. Song Jiang ordered Li Kui, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun to charge. The three to five hundred rebel soldiers guarding the road were all slain by Li Kui and the others. Around the fourth watch, they reached Dongguan. Wu Yingxing, the commander guarding that place, heard that the Song army had broken through to Dongguan. Reflecting that he had only two thousand troops under him and could never withstand the enemy, he and all his men promptly fled in a panic. He went straight back to Muzhou and reported to Chancellor Zu and the others: “Song Jiang’s troops have secretly crossed by a narrow path, passed to this side of Black Dragon Ridge, and have all reached Dongguan.” Zu Shiyuan was greatly alarmed at the news and hurriedly assembled the commanders to deliberate. Song Jiang had already ordered the artilleryman Ling Zhen to fire a rapid succession of cannon shots. In the stronghold atop Black Dragon Ridge, Shi Bao and the others were greatly alarmed by the sound. They quickly sent Commander Bai Qin with troops to investigate, and he saw Song Jiang’s banners covering heaven and earth and filling all the mountain forests. Bai Qin hastily withdrew to the stronghold on the ridge and reported to Shi Bao and the others. Shi Bao said, “Even if the court sends no reinforcements, we need only hold the pass firmly. We must not go to the rescue.” Deng Yuanjue replied, “Marshal, you are mistaken. If we do not dispatch troops to relieve Muzhou now, we may indeed choose as we please. But should the inner palace be lost, we ourselves will not remain secure. If you will not go, I shall go myself to relieve Muzhou.” Shi Bao pleaded earnestly with him, but could not dissuade him. Deng Yuanjue mustered five thousand troops, snatched up his priest’s staff, and led Xiahou Cheng down from the ridge.

p.src: Now Song Jiang, having led his army to Dongguan, did not proceed to attack Muzhou but first turned to seize the pass at Black Dragon Ridge—and there he ran directly into Deng Yuanjue. As the troops drew near, the two armies faced one another, and Deng Yuanjue rode out first to issue a challenge. Seeing him, Hua Rong whispered in Song Jiang’s ear, “This man can only be taken if we do thus and so.” Song Jiang nodded his assent. He then gave instructions to Qin Ming, and both commanders understood the plan. Qin Ming was the first to ride out and engage Deng Yuanjue. After five or six bouts, Qin Ming wheeled his horse and fled, while the troops scattered east and west. Seeing that Qin Ming was beaten, Deng Yuanjue abandoned his pursuit of him and charged straight at Song Jiang to capture him. Hua Rong had already prepared himself to protect Song Jiang. He waited until Deng Yuanjue drew fairly close, then drew his bow to the full, took careful aim, and sent an arrow whistling straight at his face. The bow bent like the full moon and the arrow flew like a meteor, striking Deng Yuanjue squarely in the face. He fell from his horse and was killed by the soldiers. The Song troops swept forward as one and closed in for the kill. The southern army suffered a crushing defeat, and Xiahou Cheng, unable to withstand them, fled toward Muzhou. The Song troops fought their way up to Black Dragon Ridge, but rolling logs and cannon stones came crashing down upon them, and they could advance no farther. The Song troops therefore turned back and went first to attack Muzhou.

p.src: Now Chancellor Zu saw the leading general Xiahou Cheng flee back and report, “The Song troops have already crossed Dongguan and killed Imperial Preceptor Deng. They will attack Muzhou any day now.” On hearing this, Zu Shiyuan sent a man with Xiahou Cheng to the imperial palace at Qingxi to ask Chancellor Lou to appear at court and memorialize: “The Song troops have now slipped along a byway into Dongguan and are pressing their attack upon Muzhou. I beg Your Majesty to dispatch troops swiftly to its relief; if there is any delay, the city will surely fall.” Fang La was greatly alarmed when he heard this. He urgently summoned Zheng Biao, Grand Commandant of the Palace Guard, placed fifteen thousand imperial guards and cavalry under his command, and ordered him to hasten through the night to relieve Muzhou. Zheng Biao memorialized, “Your servant accepts the imperial command, but begs that the Celestial Master accompany us and lend his aid, so that we may withstand Song Jiang.” Fang La approved the request and summoned Bao Daoyi, the Numinous Celestial Master. The summons was issued at once, and the Celestial Master came directly before the throne to have audience with the sovereign. Bao Daoyi bowed his head in Taoist obeisance. Fang La delivered his command: “Song Jiang’s forces are now on the verge of invading our realm and have repeatedly taken our cities and destroyed our officers and men. At this very moment, the Song troops have all reached Muzhou. We look to you, Celestial Master, to display the power of the Way, defend the country, and save the people, thereby preserving our realm and dynasty.” Celestial Master Bao replied, “Set Your Majesty’s mind at ease. Though this humble Taoist is of little ability, I shall rely upon the learning within my breast and Your Majesty’s boundless good fortune to sweep away Song Jiang’s forces.” Fang La was delighted, granted him a seat, and gave a banquet in his honor. When the banquet was over, Bao Daoyi took leave of the emperor and departed from court. Celestial Master Bao then conferred with Zheng Biao and Xiahou Cheng about mobilizing the army. After Song Jiang and Wu Yong had finished their devotions, they descended the steps and examined the stone stele. It said that the god had been a presented scholar of the Tang dynasty, surnamed Shao and named Jun. He had failed the imperial examination and died after falling into the river.
The Heavenly Emperor, pitying his loyalty and uprightness, appointed him a dragon god.
Whenever the local people prayed for wind, wind came; whenever they prayed for rain, rain fell. Therefore they built this temple and offered sacrifices in every season.

p.src: Song Jiang hastily asked the Military Adviser to interpret his dream and told him all that had happened. Wu Yong said, “Since the Dragon Lord has manifested his divine power so plainly, we may advance tomorrow and attack Muzhou.” Song Jiang said, “Your words are entirely right!” At daybreak, he issued his military orders, mustered the main body of troops, and set out to seize Muzhou. He first dispatched Yan Shun and Ma Lin to guard the main road through Wulong Ridge; then he ordered the four chief generals Guan Sheng, Hua Rong, Qin Ming, and Zhu Tong to lead the advance against Muzhou and attack its northern gate; and he ordered Ling Zhen to fire the Nine-Chambered Mother-and-Child Cannon and other artillery straight into the city. The cannonballs flew forth with a roar that seemed to split heaven and earth and shake mountains and peaks. The soldiers and horses within the city were terrified out of their wits and fell into disorder before anyone had even attacked them. Now Heavenly Master Bao and Demon Lord Zheng’s rearguard had already been scattered by Lu Zhishen, who had pursued Xiahou Cheng until his whereabouts became unknown. By then they had withdrawn their troops into the city and stationed them there. They consulted with Right Chancellor Zu Shiyuan, Administrative Councillor Shen Shou, Assistant Secretary Huan Yi, Marshal Tan Gao, garrison commander Wu Yingxing, and the others, saying, “The Song army has arrived. How are we to escape this peril?” Zu Shiyuan said, “From ancient times, when an army has reached the walls and its generals have come to the moat, how can the danger be resolved without fighting to the death? If the city is breached, we shall certainly be captured. The situation is desperate; every one of us must go forward!” At once Demon Lord Zheng led Tan Gao, Wu Yingxing, and more than ten subordinate officers, together with ten thousand picked troops, opened the city gates, and went out to confront Song Jiang. Song Jiang ordered his troops to withdraw by half an arrow’s flight, allowing the enemy to leave the city and draw up their ranks. Heavenly Master Bao took a folding chair and seated himself atop the city wall. Chancellor Zu, Administrative Councillor Shen, and Assistant Secretary Huan all sat in the gate tower to watch. Demon Lord Zheng leveled his spear, spurred his horse, and rode out from the formation. From Song Jiang’s ranks, Guan Sheng of the Great Saber rode forth, brandishing his blade, to fight Zheng Biao. The two generals crossed horses, but after only a few bouts Zheng Biao proved no match for Guan Sheng. He could do no more than parry and fend off the blows, dodging from side to side. Bao Daoyi, watching from atop the wall, now employed his sorcery. Muttering an incantation, he shouted, “Begone!” He recited the assisting spell and blew out a breath. A stream of black vapor rolled up above Demon Lord Zheng’s head, and within it appeared a golden-armored divine warrior, holding a demon-subduing jeweled pestle, which he swung downward from the sky. A murky black cloud billowed up amid the southern army. When Song Jiang saw this, he summoned Fan Rui, the Demon King Who Roils the World, to examine it. He urgently ordered him to work his magic while he himself recited the secret incantation from the Heavenly Books for turning back the wind and dispelling darkness. At once a stream of white cloud rose above Guan Sheng’s helmet. Within it there likewise appeared a divine general, red-haired and blue-faced, with emerald eyes and protruding fangs. Riding a black dragon and wielding an iron hammer, he went to fight the golden-armored divine warrior above Demon Lord Zheng’s head. Below, the two armies raised battle cries as the two generals clashed through countless bouts. Then the celestial general riding the black dragon above drove back the golden-armored divine warrior; and below, Guan Sheng cut Demon Lord Zheng from his horse with a single stroke. Bao Daoyi saw the wind rise and thunder resound among the Song forces. Just as he was hastily about to stand, Ling Zhen fired a Heaven-Shaking Cannon. A fireball struck Heavenly Master Bao squarely, smashing his head and body to pieces. The southern troops suffered a crushing defeat, and the Song forces swept into Muzhou on the strength of their momentum. Zhu Tong thrust Marshal Tan Gao from his horse with a spear, while Li Ying killed the garrison commander Wu Yingxing with a flying dagger. At the walls of Muzhou, when they saw a cannon shot strike Heavenly Master Bao’s body, all the southern soldiers tumbled down from the walls. Song Jiang’s troops had already fought their way into the city, and all his generals pressed forward together. They captured Chancellor Zu, Administrative Councillor Shen, and Assistant Secretary Huan alive; all the other subordinate officers, regardless of name, were killed by the Song soldiers. After Song Jiang and the others entered the city, they first set fire to Fang La’s temporary palace. They distributed all its gold and silks among the officers and men of the three armies, then posted proclamations to reassure the people.
